:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Using the Power of Quotient Rule with One Fraction

:question/worked-solution:
First, we apply the power of quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{-2x}{5})}^{3}=\frac{(-2x)^{3}}{{5}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power of product rule and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(-2x)^{3}}{{5}^{3}} &= \frac{(-2)^{3}{x}^{3}}{125} \\ &= -\frac{8{x}^{3}}{125}\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Using the Power of Quotient Rule with One Fraction

:question/problem: Find the value of $c$ such that $\frac{1}{2}{\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right)}^{2}=c{x}^{2}.$
:question/worked-solution:
First, we apply the power of quotient rule to the left side of the equality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right)}^{2} &=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{(2x)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power of product rule and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{(2x)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} &= \frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{{2}^{2}{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}} \\ &= \frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{4{x}^{2}}{9} \\ &= \frac{4{x}^{2}}{18} \\ &= \frac{2{x}^{2}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$c=\frac{2}{9}.$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Using the Power of Quotient Rule with Two Fractions

:question/worked-solution:
First, we apply the power of quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{4x})}^{2}{(\frac{-2x}{5})}^{3}=\frac{{3}^{2}}{(4x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{(-2x)^{3}}{{5}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the power of product rule and multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{3}^{2}}{(4x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{(-2x)^{3}}{{5}^{3}} &= \frac{{3}^{2}}{{4}^{2}{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{(-2)^{3}{x}^{3}}{{5}^{3}} \\ &= \frac{9}{16{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{-8{x}^{3}}{125} \\ &= \frac{-8\cdot 9{x}^{3}}{16\cdot 125{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we apply the quotient rule and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-8\cdot 9{x}^{3}}{16\cdot 125{x}^{2}} &= -\frac{9{x}^{3-2}}{2\cdot 125} \\ &= -\frac{9x}{250}\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_canonical-example.:knowledge-point/title: Using the Power of Quotient Rule with Two Fractions

:question/worked-solution:
First, we apply the power of quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{y}{2})}^{3}{(\frac{2y}{3})}^{2}=\frac{{y}^{3}}{{2}^{3}}\cdot \frac{(2y)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the power rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{3}}{{2}^{3}}\cdot \frac{(2y)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} &= \frac{{y}^{3}}{8}\cdot \frac{{2}^{2}{y}^{2}}{9} \\ &= \frac{{y}^{3}}{8}\cdot \frac{4{y}^{2}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we apply the product rule and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{3}}{8}\cdot \frac{4{y}^{2}}{9} &= \frac{4{y}^{(3+2)}}{72} \\ &= \frac{4{y}^{5}}{72} \\ &= \frac{{y}^{5}}{18}\end{aligned}
$$
